questions.solution:

questions.question:
What will come in the place of the question mark ‘(?)’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged?

69 − 2 ÷ 7 + 35 × 7 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/952c967501c582f1911db7fefdaaefa9b6e3f505512624eb925e04e002be5a1f.png] 

Given: 69 − 2 ÷ 7 + 35 × 7 = ?

According to the question, after ‘÷’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged:

69 − 2 ÷ 7 + 35 × 7 = ? ⇒ 69 + 2 × 7 − 35 ÷ 7 = ?

⇒ 69 + 2 × 7 − __**35 **____**÷**____** 7**__ = ?

⇒ 69 + __**2 **____**×**____** 7**__ − 5 = ?

⇒ __**69 + 14**__ − 5 = ?

⇒ __**83**____** − 5**__ = ?

⇒ 78 = ?

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two different positions of the same dice are given below. Which is the number on the face opposite to the face containing 2?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4a6e4898e22aac4d00cd637c21ab94c358bbfad1e3f8022646b9e202e8673e2.png]
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

From the given two different cubes the adjacent sides are as shown below :

As 6 is common on both the dices, it is clear that 5, 4, 1, and 3 are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. 2 will be opposite to it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c49f94ad8bf3fb6a1a99f7c382da3559f19cc8c51b1f2aec28dba5d06f392da.png] 

Opposite pairs:

4 → 3

5 → 1

6 → 2

So, the opposite side of "2" will be side "6".

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
G, H, I, J, K, L and M are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table(but not necessarily in the same order) .

Only one person sits between M and L when counted from the right of M. Only one person sits between L and I. Only one person sits between M and H. Only two people sit between K and I. Only one person sits between J and H.

Who sits to the immediate right and left of G, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given: G, H, I, J, K, L and M are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table.

​​1) Only one person sits between M and L when counted from the right of M. 

2) Only one person sits between M and H.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32237338a0425663c4d3c338530b9a89897b65b7d50b4d21dda69a4e2aaa6eb0.png] 

3) Only two people sit between K and I.

4) Only one person sits between L and I.

5) Only one person sits between J and H.

After positioning all only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36627e4884a0ba4a3cf3f5a49ea395f146222f529c6e5fa111f7227d9ca5c4db.png] 

Thus, M and H sits to the immediate right and left of G respectively.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
In a certain code language,

'A + B' means 'A is the father of B',

'A - B' means 'A is the wife of B',

'A x B' means 'A is the brother of B' and

'A ÷ B' means 'A is the daughter of B'.

How is F related to C if 'C - D x E ÷ F + G'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b1887e263a0be106c3fc3bef05d4c58742c6a15e36b93bc74e9b8034e1f5d249.png]

Given Expression: C - D x E ÷ F + G

C - D → C is the wife of D. 

D x E → D is the brother of E.

E ÷ F → E is the daughter of F.

F + G → F is the father of G. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a083603ce2a980e3b47d7127f6d176bb4150524f17a0179cc0c60f44b165b4a.png] 

Thus, F is C's husband’s father.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All pants are trousers.

No pant is a shirt.

All shirts are coats.

Conclusions:

(I): No coat is a trouser.

(II): Some coats are pants
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc3823792b6b34103f3e550c40c836afd45e10f28dabc017565696f7416d64b8.png] 

Conclusions:

(I): No coat is a trouser → Does not follow (As all pants are trousers, no pant is a shirt and all shirts are coats. As no direct relation is given between coat and trouser, therefore it is false.)

(II): Some coats are pants → Does not follow (As no pant is a shirt and all shirts are coats. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows. ​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
